title: From Abstraction to Action: DSLs for Natural Language Abstraction Interpretation and Execution
abstract: arXiv:2610.28311v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural-language instructions often rely on high-level abstractions, such as asking an agent to ``stack blocks in a pyramid.'' Interpreting abstract instructions requires models to both identify the abstraction intended by the speaker, and unroll it into the many concrete actions that instantiate it. Language models struggle here: prior work has shown that performance degrades as the level of abstraction in the instruction rises. To bridge the gap between natural language abstraction and concrete actions, we propose to borrow from coding environments the notion of a {\em domain-specific language} (DSL), an explicit representation layer whose documented primitives name recurring abstractions that expand into concrete actions. We demonstrate the efficacy of DSLs for NL interpretation on \textsc{Hexagons}, a visually-grounded instruction-following task graded for abstraction. We further ask whether language models can induce such DSLs thems

translated_title: 从抽象到行动：用于自然语言抽象解释与执行的领域特定语言（DSL）
translated_abstract: 自然语言指令通常依赖于高层次的抽象，例如让智能体“把积木堆成金字塔”。解释抽象指令需要模型既能识别说话者所意图的抽象，又能将其展开为实现该抽象的许多具体动作。语言模型在这方面表现不佳：先前的研究表明，随着指令抽象层次的提高，模型性能会下降。为了弥合自然语言抽象与具体动作之间的差距，我们提出借鉴编程环境中的领域特定语言（DSL）概念——这是一种显式表示层，其文档化的原语为反复出现的抽象命名，并可将这些抽象展开为具体动作。我们在 Hexagons 上展示了 DSL 在自然语言解释方面的有效性，这是一个按抽象程度分级、以视觉为基础的指令遵循任务。我们进一步探究语言模型能否自行归纳出这样的 DSL。
tldr: 本文提出借鉴编程领域的领域特定语言（DSL）作为显式抽象表示层，使语言模型能够识别高抽象层次的自然语言指令并将其展开为具体可执行的动作。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes borrowing domain-specific languages (DSLs) from programming as an explicit abstraction representation layer, enabling language models to identify high-level abstract natural language instructions and unroll them into concrete executable actions.
